text: Depending on what an organization does and what data its instance touches, several real frameworks commonly come up. SOC 2 is a set of trust service criteria customers and auditors commonly expect of any SaaS vendor. HIPAA matters the moment protected health information is involved. GDPR applies to any EU individual's personal data, regardless of where the organization is headquartered. PCI-DSS matters if payment card data ever touches the instance, even indirectly.

Here's the single most important idea in this lesson: ServiceNow the platform provides capabilities that help meet these frameworks. It does not make an implementation automatically compliant just because the organization runs on it. Encryption, audit logging, ACLs, masking, export controls — every one of these is a capability the platform makes available.

Whether any of it is actually configured correctly, applied to the right data, reviewed on a real cadence, and operated consistently is the customer's responsibility. Capability existing is not the same thing as compliance being achieved — that gap is entirely configuration and operation, and it's customer-side.

A stakeholder will sometimes ask, in effect, doesn't ServiceNow just handle compliance for us. The honest answer is no — using a bank vault doesn't automatically mean a company's financial controls are sound. The vault is a real, strong tool. Whether it's actually used correctly is what determines the outcome.

Concretely, SOC 2's security and confidentiality criteria lean on the ACL and encryption work from earlier chapters. HIPAA's requirement to track who accessed PHI-adjacent records leans directly on the selective audit logging from Lesson 19.

GDPR's data-subject rights lean on being able to locate, export, and erase a specific person's data — which depends on the attachment and export controls from Chapter 4 being configured deliberately. PCI-DSS leans on the same combination of field-level security, masking, and audit logging, applied to cardholder data specifically.

None of these frameworks are satisfied by one feature in isolation. Each depends on several of this course's capabilities being configured together, correctly, for the specific data that framework cares about. Lesson 21 works through exactly that, end to end, for a real healthcare scenario.
